name: Can you get a flat-price quote for pool fill-in?

mainEntity.name: Do pool fill-in contractors in Los Angeles ever offer a flat-price quote?
mainEntity.text: Do pool fill-in contractors in Los Angeles ever offer a flat-price quote?

acceptedAnswer.text: A flat-price quote can work for simple pool fill-in jobs, but only if the contractor has enough information to price the work accurately. If the yard has easy access, the pool size is standard, and the scope is straightforward, a flat quote may be possible. Complicated access, unknown utilities, permit uncertainty, or unclear compaction requirements make flat pricing risky for both sides. That is why many homeowners do better with an itemized proposal that shows demolition, export, backfill, compaction, grading, and permit-related costs separately. Itemized pricing makes it easier to see whether one bid is actually cheaper or just incomplete. If a contractor offers a flat price, the homeowner should confirm exactly what is included and what counts as a change order. The best quote is the one that clearly defines the scope, not just the number at the bottom.
acceptedAnswer.description: Some contractors offer flat-price quotes, but only when access, pool size, demolition scope, hauling distance, and permit requirements are clear. Flat pricing is harder for complicated sites because hidden conditions can change the cost. An itemized estimate is usually safer and easier to compare.
